NJ-04.path_note: AL/MC is not in the approved 305-unit age-restricted plan, which is tied to the borough's fourth-round fair share plan. Adding a care pad means amending that plan and the site plan, with Garden Homes as partner and a DOH expedited CN running in parallel.
NJ-04.likelihood_note: High. The borough already accepted senior housing on this site in its fair share plan and approved Arbor Terrace's 100-bed AL in 2024. Opposition is low to medium. The open question is whether Garden Homes and the borough will reopen an approval the town relies on for affordable-housing compliance.

methods: Approach Garden Homes first with a pad purchase or JV that does not reduce their affordable-unit count. The borough's fair share compliance rides on this site, so any amendment must keep or add credits.
Offer the 10% Medicaid AL beds the CN requires as additional fair share credit, subject to the age-restricted cap, and position the pad as helping the borough's compliance.

Hold a staff meeting with the Administrative Officer and the Borough Engineer before a concept plan goes to the Planning Board. Ask them which instrument applies: a fair share plan amendment, a redevelopment plan amendment or an amended site plan.
Brief Mayor Taylor and the council president before filing. Any change to the fair share plan goes back through the governing body and the court-approved compliance process.
sources: https://www.florhamparknj.gov/media/Public Notices/2026/2026-01-25 - Florham Park - Amended Housing Element and Fair Share Plan.pdf

NJ-06.path_note: OB-RL3 permits licensed nursing homes and hospitals (2019 code). Before any amendment, ask the zoning officer for a written determination, or the Zoning Board for an interpretation under N.J.S.A. 40:55D-70b, that licensed AL/MC falls within that health-care use. If it does not, add AL as a permitted or conditional use in the JMF plan.
NJ-06.likelihood_note: High. The health-care use is already permitted in the zone, opposition is low, and the township has worked with JMF on 400 homes and a hotel. The risk is a narrow reading of 'nursing home' that excludes assisted living.

methods: Ask for a zoning officer's determination first. It is cheap, fast and appealable, and it can turn an amendment path into a site-plan-only path.
Structure the deal with JMF as a pad sale with shared infrastructure and reciprocal easements, so the AL/MC rides on their access, utilities and stormwater approvals.
Frame the use as health care, not housing: licensed beds and clinical staff fit the OB-RL3 purpose next to the township's office and medical base.
Meet with the Land Use Office to confirm the Planning Board's submission checklist and escrow, and whether the township planner will support an interpretation.

NJ-10.path_note: Brookside at Montville was approved by the Zoning Board of Adjustment (5-2, 18 variances, 10/4/2023) and appealed by Montville Residents for Responsible Growth LLC. Diversified closed title in March 2026. Adding AL/MC means amending that use-variance approval at the Zoning Board, which needs 5 of 7 votes and reopens the record to the same objectors. Montville is in the Highlands region, so Highlands consistency also applies.
NJ-10.likelihood_note: Moderate. The board has approved senior use here, but by a variance and over organized, funded opposition that appealed. A care component draws less traffic than the 266 units, but any amendment invites a second challenge.

methods: Confirm the status of the 2023 appeal before any LOI. Do not file an amendment while the original approval is being litigated.
Build the amendment on lower impact: AL/MC trips are a fraction of the 266 units, and placing the care building on the already-disturbed footprint avoids new wetlands or conservation-area impacts.
Meet with the objectors' leadership before the Zoning Board does. Offer a conservation and tree-replacement package and a construction traffic plan.
Use Diversified's existing professionals and approved stormwater design, so the board reviews a delta rather than a new project.

NY-10.path_note: Hudson Heritage's approved master plan includes assisted living. The pad needs Planning Board site plan approval within the approved plan, and SEQRA consistency with the master plan's findings, so a new EIS is not needed if the program fits the envelope. DOH ALR / EALR licensure runs in parallel.
NY-10.likelihood_note: High. The use and density are already approved, the master developer is building, and town staff are professionally led. The main risk is commercial: pad pricing and timing with EFG/Saber.

methods: Negotiate the pad with EFG/Saber on a finished-pad basis (utilities, access and stormwater delivered) so the town reviews only the building.
Meet with Michael Welti to confirm the program fits the master plan's SEQRA findings statement. If it does, the Planning Board can act on a consistency determination with no new EIS.
File the DOH ALR / EALR application at schematic design. Licensure is usually the longer pole than the site plan here.
Present the project as the care component the town already approved, so the board is completing its own plan.

NY-03.path_note: The Medical Oriented District (2023) encourages AL, IL and SNF across from NYP Hudson Valley Hospital. VS Construction's 96,850 SF assisted living at 2003 Crompond Road is in a Planning Board public hearing for site plan approval plus tree, wetland and steep-slope permits. The hearing was adjourned on 5/5/2026 to 6/2/2026 over stormwater, a retaining wall and fire access.
NY-03.likelihood_note: High on use, medium on timing. The town created the district for this use. The open items are technical, not about the use itself, but neighbors along Route 202 have pushed back on MOD projects generally.

methods: Track the 6/2/2026 and later hearings. Once stormwater and fire access close, the approval is buildable, and buying it with the site is cheaper than re-entitling.
If you partner rather than buy, keep the existing team (Zarin & Steinmetz, DTS Provident). They hold the board's confidence and the full record.
Close the LaBella and Fire Advisory Board comments in writing before each hearing. This board adjourns rather than denies when technical items stay open.
Frame the project around the hospital across the street and the Envision Cortlandt plan the town adopted unanimously.

CT-02.path_note: The Planning & Zoning Commission approved a zone change and text amendments in January 2019 (Silver Heights Development) and later a site plan 4-1, after a three-year process that included an appeal and an Inland Wetlands approval. Confirm vesting and expiry: CGS 8-3(i) gives 5 years to complete site plan work, extendable. Then file any program changes as a site plan modification, and negotiate a CGS 12-65b tax abatement with the Town Council.
CT-02.likelihood_note: High. The use is decided and the record is built. The risks are an expired or lapsed approval and the town's current posture: Trumbull leadership has publicly fought state housing mandates, so do not frame the project as housing policy.

methods: Before price talks, get the approval resolutions, the wetlands permit and any extensions from the Land Use Planner, and confirm with the ZEO that they are vested and unexpired.
Keep any changes inside the approved envelope (units, height, footprint) so they go to staff or the Commission as a minor modification, not a new public hearing.
Frame the deal as reuse of an empty office building with taxes, jobs and no school children. Avoid affordable-housing framing given the town's stance on state mandates.
Negotiate the 12-65b abatement with the First Selectman's office alongside the purchase, since it decides the fully taxed versus structured yield.

NY-01.path_note: The 900 King Street PUD is approved and in hand. The Planning Board adopted a second-amended SEQRA finding and an amended PUD site plan on 5/14/2026, with no change in units or bedrooms and conditions on the school easement, path and construction management. What remains: the Architectural Review Board, a construction management plan and building permits. Sunrise Senior Living came in as contract vendee in October 2024.
NY-01.likelihood_note: Very high on entitlement, since it is approved. The practical question is access to the deal: Sunrise is under contract. The village is also running a positive-declaration SEQR review of Erickson Living's 834-unit senior PUD at 975 Anderson Hill Road, which confirms appetite for senior use but adds competing supply.

methods: Approach the owner and Sunrise about taking a JV or capital position rather than competing for the site, since the entitlement is spoken for.
If the Sunrise contract lapses, move fast. The approval and the 5/14/2026 amended findings are the asset, and The Arbors relationship comes with it.
Keep a standing line to the Village Administrator. The village extends approvals in exchange for monthly progress reporting.
Watch the Erickson DEIS. If it advances, use it in the market study as both validation and competing supply.
